title: This Portfolio: Full-stack Platform with a Visual Site Builder, AI Assistant & CMS
description: The site you're on, built end to end by me: a Next.js 16 + TypeScript platform with a mobile-first CMS, a Shopify-style drag-and-drop site builder with templates and one-click publish, an “Ask my resume” AI assistant that works with Claude, OpenAI, Gemini and more, role-based security, analytics and SEO.
objective: Build a portfolio that works like a real product instead of a static page: recruiters get what they need in seconds (role, availability, contact, resume, answers to their questions), and I can update content, change the whole design or switch AI providers from my phone in a minute, with no code change or redeploy. Constraints: fast, secure, accessible, and running on free hosting tiers.
approach:
Server Components render every page straight from the database, so edits go live on the next page load. One set of Zod schemas validates both the admin forms and the REST API.

Security is layered: scrypt-hashed passwords, signed HttpOnly session tokens that are revoked on password change, a single proxy in front of /admin and /api, login rate limiting, admin and editor roles with a protected owner account, and uploads checked by their real file content.

The design system is data: pages are stored as JSON and rendered on the server from an allow-listed set of blocks. Themes are CSS variables, so one setting restyles the whole site. The AI layer is provider-agnostic, with encrypted keys and automatic fallback.
architecture:
Visitor / Recruiter          Admin (phone or laptop)
        │                         │
        ▼                         ▼
   Next.js 16 on Vercel ─ proxy.ts (auth + roles)
   ├─ Server Components → pages, SEO, JSON-LD
   ├─ Design renderer  → JSON layout → blocks
   ├─ REST API (Zod)   → CMS, uploads, design,
   │                     AI providers, insights
   └─ Visual editor (Puck) → draft → publish
        │ Prisma 7 + libSQL
        ▼
   Turso (hosted SQLite)
        │
   AI providers (fallback order)
   Claude · OpenAI · Gemini · Groq · …
result: Everything on the site (content, photos, resume, layout, colors, AI provider) is editable from a phone, and design changes go live instantly without a redeploy. The editable “Classic” template renders pixel-identical to the hand-built homepage (0 of 8.6 million pixels differ on desktop and phone). The site builder is covered by 48 automated API checks, including role, validation and XSS cases. It runs on free tiers; an AI answer on Claude Haiku costs about $0.003, with daily and per-visitor limits keeping the bill predictable.
content:
## Why I built it
A portfolio is usually the first thing a recruiter opens, and most are static pages that go stale. I wanted mine to prove the skills it describes: product thinking, UX, frontend, backend, security, AI and DevOps, all in one real, running system that I use every day.

## What recruiters get
- Hiring snapshot at the top: target roles, location and work mode, availability and notice period
- One-tap contact: email, copy email (for webmail users) and LinkedIn, plus a resume PDF download
- “Ask my resume”: an AI chat that answers questions using only what's on the site, so it doesn't make things up
- Case studies and articles for every project, with drafts hidden until they're ready
- Fast, SEO-friendly pages with structured data (JSON-LD), sitemap, share images and canonical URLs
- A gaming-inspired interface with controller-style A/B/X/Y shortcuts, plus a one-click switch to a clean, professional light theme

## Admin panel: a mobile-first CMS
- Edit profile, experience, skills, projects, all site text and the resume from a phone
- Photo uploads resized in the browser (including iPhone photos) before upload
- Three project types: case study, article, or direct link, with featured, drafts and reorder
- Site text supports placeholders such as {years} and {level}, calculated from the profile
- Backup: export and import everything as JSON, or add and update projects from JSON
- Insights: resume downloads, contact clicks and AI questions (7 days, 30 days, all time) without storing IPs or cookies, plus Vercel Web Analytics for page views

## Visual site builder: Shopify-style, no code
- Drag-and-drop editor built on Puck, with phone, tablet and desktop previews
- 5 templates: Classic (the original site, pixel-identical but fully editable), Arcade, Minimal, Studio and Blank
- 29 blocks: live-data blocks (hero, projects, experience, skills, contact…), classic sections, and layout and text blocks (sections, columns, cards, headings, images, buttons)
- Page settings: 7 color themes, all 9 palette colors with color pickers, fonts, text size, heading style, corners, button shape and style, page width, and right-to-left text
- Style on every block: background color or image, text, accent and card colors, spacing, width, corners, border, shadow, and show on phone or desktop only
- Autosaved drafts, full-page preview, one-click publish, revert to live, and the last 5 published versions can be restored
- Content still comes from the CMS, so changing the design never loses or duplicates data
- The server validates every design: only known blocks, size and nesting limits, and only safe links and image URLs

## AI assistant, provider-agnostic
- Add, remove, reorder and test any provider: Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI, Google Gemini, Groq, OpenRouter, Mistral, DeepSeek or any OpenAI-compatible API
- Automatic fallback: if one provider fails (bad key, out of credit, down), the next one answers
- API keys are encrypted (AES-256-GCM) before storage, and only the last 4 characters are ever shown again
- Cost controls: questions per day, per visitor every 10 minutes, and maximum answer length; prompt caching on Claude

## Security and access
- scrypt password hashing, and signed HttpOnly sessions revoked when the password changes
- One proxy guards all admin pages and APIs; login attempts are rate limited
- Roles: admins manage users, design, AI settings and insights; editors can only edit content. The owner account can't be removed
- Admin-only API tokens for scripts; every write is validated by shared Zod schemas
- Uploads are checked by their real file content (magic bytes), not just the file name

## Engineering and operations
- Next.js 16 App Router, React 19 Server Components, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS 4
- Prisma 7 with libSQL: a SQLite file locally, Turso in production
- Additive database migrations run automatically on every Vercel deploy
- Documented REST API for every feature
- Tested with automated API checks and screenshot checks on phone and desktop

## What it shows about how I work
I owned this end to end: product decisions, UX for recruiters and for myself as the admin, frontend architecture, API design, security, AI integration, testing and deployment. It's the same approach I bring to a team: ship something real, measure it, and keep it easy to change.

title: Hybrid Code Search for a Talk-to-Code Assistant: RAG, BM25 and Re-ranking
description: Why a code assistant needs more than vector search, and how combining semantic search, BM25 keyword search and re-ranking improves the answers.
content:
## The goal
A VS Code prototype that answers questions about a codebase, right inside the editor. [Add: which codebase, who it was for.]

## Why vector search alone falls short for code
Semantic search finds code that means the same thing, but exact names (function names, config keys, error codes) often need keyword matching.

## The approach
- Index code chunks in a vector database for semantic search
- Run BM25 keyword search alongside it
- Merge the candidates and re-rank them before sending the best ones to the model (RAG)
